Warp a dataset onto a grid

Source: R/warp.R
warp_raster.Rd

Reproject and resample bands of a dataset onto a destination grid, with GDAL's warp API and no utility layer: a transformer from the source to crs (GDALCreateGenImgProjTransformer2, approximated within error_threshold pixels as gdalwarp's -et), then GDALWarpOperation::ChunkAndWarpImage into an in-memory dataset. For the same kernel and the same source, the values are gdalwarp's.

Usage

warp_raster(
  x,
  crs,
  extent,
  size,
  resample = "nearest",
  bands = NULL,
  type = "double",
  alpha_band = NULL,
  error_threshold = 0.125,
  nara = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A GDALDataset.

crs

The destination CRS, anything GDAL understands ("EPSG:3031", a PROJ string, WKT).

extent

Numeric of length 4: c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in crs.

size

Integer of length 2: the destination width and height.

resample

gdalwarp's -r names: "nearest" (or "near"), "bilinear", "cubic", "cubicspline", "lanczos", "average", "rms", "mode", "max", "min", "med", "q1", "q3", "sum".

bands

Which bands, one-based. Defaults to all of them.

type

As in read_raster(): "double", "integer" or "raw". Ignored when nara = TRUE.

alpha_band

A source band whose zeros mask the source (gdalwarp's -srcalpha). NULL (the default) does what gdalwarp does: the last band, if it is an alpha band and among bands. 0 for none. Give it explicitly for a WMS or WMTS dataset opened at an overview, whose bands report no colour interpretation (GDAL 3.14).

error_threshold

Maximum error, in pixels, of the approximate transformer. 0.125 is gdalwarp's default; 0 is exact.

nara

Return a nativeRaster instead of a list of bands.

Value

A named list of one row-major vector per band, of size[1] * size[2] values (as read_raster() returns for a dataset), or with nara = TRUE a nativeRaster of size[2] rows and size[1] columns.

Details

The source is the dataset as opened, so the resolution it is read at is the caller's choice: to warp from an overview, open it with options = "OVERVIEW_LEVEL=k only" (" only", so no coarser level is exposed). Source nodata is honoured and carried to the destination, as gdalwarp does.

With nara = TRUE the result is a nativeRaster: the warp writes four Byte bands and one GDAL read interleaves them into its four bytes per pixel, so nothing is packed in R. That needs Byte bands: one (grey) or three (RGB), plus an optional alpha band. The alpha byte is the destination alpha GDAL computes, 0 where no source pixel contributes.

Examples

ds <- gdal_open(system.file("extdata/test.tif", package = "GDAL7"))

# test.tif's own grid, at half the resolution, with bilinear resampling.
gt <- ds@geotransform
ext <- c(gt[1], gt[4] + ds@raster_ysize * gt[6], gt[1] + ds@raster_xsize * gt[2], gt[4])
v <- warp_raster(ds, ds@projection, ext, size = c(10L, 10L), resample = "bilinear")
str(v)
#> List of 2
#>  $ 1: num [1:100] 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 ...
#>  $ 2: num [1:100] 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 ...

# The same area in longitude and latitude.
ll <- transform_extent(ext, ds@projection, "EPSG:4326")
str(warp_raster(ds, "EPSG:4326", ll, size = c(8L, 8L)))
#> List of 2
#>  $ 1: num [1:64] 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 ...
#>  $ 2: num [1:64] 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 7 ...
gdal_close(ds)

# An RGB image warped straight into a nativeRaster.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
rgb <- gdal_create(path, 16, 16, bands = 3, type = "Byte")
rgb@geotransform <- c(0, 1, 0, 16, 0, -1)
rgb@projection <- "EPSG:32755"
write_raster(rgb, lapply(1:3, function(b) as.double(rep(b * 60, 256))))
gdal_close(rgb)
ds <- gdal_open(path)
n <- warp_raster(ds, "EPSG:32755", c(-4, -4, 20, 20), size = c(24L, 24L), nara = TRUE)
class(n)
#> [1] "nativeRaster"
if (interactive()) plot(as.raster(n))
gdal_close(ds)
unlink(path)
